item.title: Tope Alabi threatens legal action over online defamation

The warning was contained in a public notice issued by her lawyers, Oakmount Legal Practitioners, and shared on the singer’s Instagram page on Friday, October 23, 2026. item.title: 2027: Wike debunks viral post backing Adamawa LP candidate, Abbo
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi Minister of the Federal Capital Territory FCT, Nyesom Wike, has debunked a social media post claiming he is backing Senator Ishaku Abbo, the Labour Party LP candidate in next year’s Adamawa State governorship election. Wike, who spoke through his Senior Special Assistant on Public Communications and Social Media, Lere Olayinka, described the report as fake. Olayinka said the minister has no relationship with the LP or any of its candidates in Adamawa State. The post in question quoted Wike as urging the people of Adamawa State to make informed and thoughtful decisions at the ballot, adding that, in his opinion, Abbo is best fit to lead the state. The minister, however, said he did not at any time endorse Abbo or any other LP candidate. He urged the people of Adamawa State to disregard the post, stressing that whoever he is supporting, he will say so with his own mouth. item.description: US First Lady Melania Trump said in a surprise announcement Friday she had secured a localized ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine in the ravaged city of Oleshky, where citizens are trapped and short of food. The localized ceasefire in Russian-occupied Oleshky would begin on October 29, a statement issued by her office said. There was no immediate confirmation from Moscow or Kyiv. “The situation in Oleshky is dire. Oleshky is a front-line war city on the brink of disaster,” Melania, the wife of President Donald Trump, said in the statement. “It was abundantly clear that without my intervention, the possibility to bring humanitarian aid into the city and to evacuate the elderly would be impossible.” The announcement comes a year after the Slovenian-born former model stunned the world by revealing she had established a back channel of communication with Russian President Vladimir Putin. Melania Trump has since secured the “reunifications” of 34 children separated from their parents by the war, her office said. In a number of cases they had been abducted by Russia. item.title: 2027: Tinubu’s aide claims CityBoy Movement has support across party lines
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Senior Special Assistant to President Bola Tinubu on Digital/New Media, O’tega Ogra, has claimed that the CityBoy Movement has been welcomed by a majority of Nigerian youths and has attracted members across party lines, including from opposition parties, ahead of the 2027 general election. Ogra, who is also Deputy Director-General of the CityBoy Movement, a group campaigning in support of President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid, made the claim on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Thursday while responding to questions about the movement’s reach and acceptance among young Nigerians. When asked about areas where the movement had yet to gain acceptance, Ogra said he was open to discussing any such areas but maintained that the movement had received support from a majority of Nigerian youths. “I mean, if you show me one, I might be able to speak to that. But as far as I know, we have been welcomed by a majority of Nigerian youths,” he said. Ogra also claimed that the movement had members across the political divide, including people associated with major opposition parties. “We’re a movement that has members across the political space. We have members from the PDP. We have members from Alhaji Atiku’s own party. We have members that have come from Peter Obi’s own party. We have members who belong to Seyi Makinde’s government within our structure,” he said. Explaining what he believed was driving the movement’s appeal among young Nigerians, Ogra said youths were tired of political leaders who, in his view, made promises they failed to keep and diverted public funds for private interests. “Because at the end of the day, the Nigerian youths, we are done with people telling us lies. We are done with people promising one thing and putting government funds into their private enterprise,” he said. He further argued that young Nigerians were better equipped to scrutinise political leaders because of their access to information and fact-checking tools. “We’re done with people, you know, trying to play on our intelligence. We are smarter than whatever was in the 1990s or in the 2000s. We have access to news, we have access to information, we can fact check, we can revalidate, we have these things at our fingertips and one thing that we have chosen to do at the City Boy movement, our motto is inform, engage, empower,” Ogra added. item.title: Shun partisan politics, Aiyedatiwa tells Ondo corps members
item.description: By Dayo Johnson Akure Governor Lucky Aiyedatiwa of Ondo State has charged members of the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) deployed to the state to avoid partisan politics in their host communities. Aiyedatiwa gave the charge at the closing ceremony and terminal parade of the 2026 Batch C Stream I orientation course held at Ikare-Akoko. Represented by the State Coordinator of the scheme, Mrs Kuburat Omowumi Bakare, the governor urged the corps members to be conscious of their responsibilities. “Remain mindful of the responsibilities that come with your position as corps members. Your actions will reflect not only on you but also on your families, your institutions and the NYSC,” he said. He appealed to employers and heads of establishments to receive corps members posted to them with cooperation and understanding. “Provide them with a conducive working environment, appropriate guidance and opportunities to contribute their knowledge and skills. Your mentorship can help them grow professionally and gain valuable experience that will serve them well beyond their service year,” Aiyedatiwa said. He also called on local government authorities, traditional rulers and community leaders to support corps members in their areas to aid their integration and effective execution of Community Development Service projects. “Your cooperation is essential to their successful integration into host communities and to the effective implementation of Community Development Service projects. By working together, we can ensure that the presence of corps members translates into tangible benefits for the people of Ondo State,” he added. The governor further urged the corps members to accept their postings in good faith and serve with diligence, integrity and respect for their host communities. “Approach your responsibilities with a strong sense of duty. Accept your postings in good faith and serve with diligence, integrity and respect for the people among whom you will live and work. Be willing to learn from your host communities, respect their customs and cultural values and conduct yourselves in ways that will earn their trust and confidence. “Your service year should be about more than fulfilling an obligation. It should be an opportunity to contribute meaningfully to society,” he said. Aiyedatiwa assured that his administration will continue to collaborate with security agencies and other stakeholders to ensure a safe environment for corps members throughout the service year. He cautioned them against compromising their personal security, advising them to remain vigilant, avoid late-night movements and unsafe gatherings, and shun unsolicited rides from strangers. “Be cautious when visiting unfamiliar or isolated places and promptly report suspicious activities or security concerns to the appropriate authorities. “Shun drug abuse, cybercrime, fraud and other unlawful activities that could jeopardise your future and bring disrepute to the scheme,” the governor added.

item.title: Atiku challenges Tinubu to name ministers, appointees involved in alleged bribery
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has challenged President Bola Tinubu to identify those who allegedly received billions of naira in bribes from ministers to secure appointments, following the allegation by All Progressives Congress (APC) campaign spokesperson Alwan Hassan. Atiku made the demand in a post on his X handle on Friday, questioning who received the alleged payments and criticising the Tinubu administration over the rising cost of living and the funding of ministries. “Bola @officialABAT, your campaign spokesman has admitted that ministers paid billions in bribes to secure their appointments. You appointed them, so who received the money? Nigerians deserve names, not silence,” Atiku wrote. The former vice president also blamed the administration’s decisions for the cost-of-living crisis, alleging that the government’s handling of ministry funding had left Nigerians bearing the consequences. “Your government’s reckless decisions have driven the cost-of-living crisis. And when you withhold funds from ministries because you distrust your own ministers, Nigerians are left paying for a government that has abandoned them,” he added. Bola @officialABAT , your campaign spokesman has admitted that ministers paid billions in bribes to secure their appointments. You appointed them, so who received the money? Nigerians deserve names, not silence. Your government’s reckless decisions have driven the cost-of-living… pic.twitter.com/OlNYIfOCbf — Atiku Abubakar (@atiku) October 23, 2026 Hassan, a spokesperson for the APC Presidential Campaign Council, made the allegation during an interview on Arise News on Thursday while defending Tinubu’s record ahead of the 2027 general election. He alleged that some ministers pay billions of naira to secure appointments and then focus on recovering the money after assuming office. He also maintained that the practice was not limited to the APC administration but predated the party’s time in government. “A lot of ministers pay billions to be appointed, and the first thing they think of is how to recoup that money after being appointed,” Hassan said. “It is the truth about our country and not just APC ministers; it started before the APC,” he added. Hassan did not name any minister who allegedly paid for an appointment or identify the recipients of the purported payments in the reported interview. While defending Tinubu’s administration, the APC campaign spokesperson also cited government initiatives in the power sector and education, including funding for electricity meters and the renovation of primary schools and classrooms, as examples of the administration’s performance ahead of the 2027 election. item.title: Crude oil rises to $115 with stocks mixed on earnings, AI
item.description: Oil prices traded at five-month highs on Friday, with benchmark crude contract Brent North Sea rising above $115 a barrel, as the Middle East conflict raged on. Global markets were contending “with concerns around surging oil prices and the sustainability of AI spending”, noted AJ Bell head of financial analysis Danni Hewson. “Oil is at five-month highs amid speculation there may be renewed US-Israeli strikes after next month’s US midterm elections. “Escalating tensions in Ukraine and the prospect of increased energy demand as the northern hemisphere heads into the winter months are only adding to the upwards pressure on oil and gas prices,” Hewson added. Benchmark international oil contract Brent crude for December delivery rose as high as $115.45. Wall Street’s main indices slid at the start of trading, with the blue-chip Dow sinking one percent. “The ongoing agitation of the oil market has contributed to the lack of a buy-the-dip impulse” that has often helped Wall Street stocks avoid pulling lower this year. High oil prices also “keep inflation concerns and rate hike concerns on the front burner”, he added. Higher borrowing costs would make it more expensive for companies to borrow, which could pull the rug out from under breakneck development of AI that is being financed by debt and has underpinned the rise in equity markets this year. Stock markets mostly dropped in Europe following some poorly-received earnings from Gucci parent Kering and Swedish group Volvo Cars. Asian equity indices closed out the week mixed as technology firms managed to claw back some of the week’s hefty losses. Rising energy prices have influenced movements across stock markets in recent days along with developments in the AI sector. Facebook parent Meta and chip equipment maker Lam Research saw their share prices dive this week despite above-forecast earnings for the pair. “Strong results are no longer enough if the outlook fails to match an already demanding valuation,” noted Fawad Razaqzada, a markets analyst at traders FOREX.com. “Investors are becoming much less forgiving.” Non-AI companies have also seen their share prices slump this week. Kering shed more than 16 percent in Paris afternoon deals on Friday after the French luxury group published results that failed to reassure investors about a turnaround at its key Gucci brand. Volvo Cars meanwhile plunged more than 26 percent after it said US tariffs and strong competition from local brands in China pushed it into a third-quarter loss. In response, the company announced a new five-billion-kronor savings plan it said would lead to about 2,000 job cuts in Sweden and 500 more globally. Aside from energy markets, AI and earnings next week, focus will fall firmly on interest-rate meetings for the US Federal Reserve and European Central Bank, as well as an update on US economic growth data. – Key figures at around 1330 GMT – Brent North Sea crude: UP 1.9 percent at $115.29 per barrel West Texas Intermediate: UP 2.3

item.title: Gunmen kill 7 at church in southern Jordan
item.description: Gunmen killed at least seven people and wounded 10 more in an attack on a church in southern Jordan on Friday, authorities said. Two assailants stormed the compound of a Greek Orthodox church in the village of Hammoud in Karak governorate before opening fire, the public security directorate said in a statement. “Seven people died at least… while around 10 people were wounded, some of them critically,” the directorate said. The gunmen got out of a vehicle and opened fire during a funeral procession, it added, saying that a manhunt was underway for the perpetrators. Minister of Government Communications Mohammed Al-Momani said security forces were investigating the attack. An eyewitness told the kingdom’s state broadcaster Al-Mamlaka that a vehicle arrived carrying the gunmen, who fired continuously for five minutes before fleeing the scene. Between 150 and 200 people were in and around the church at the time, the witness said, adding that most of the victims were aged between 50 and 70. item.title: Umahi accuses Obi of starting confrontation, faults his silence over supporters’ ‘Jesus’ remarks
item.description: Minister of Works David Umahi has accused former Anambra State governor Peter Obi of initiating their public disagreement, saying the Labour Party’s 2023 presidential candidate first confronted him at a construction site. In an interview with Arise News, Umahi said Obi had publicly criticised him while he was working at the site, describing the incident as unfair. “I did not criticise Peter Obi; he started the confrontation by coming to the construction site where I was working and publicly castigating me. I consider that very unfair,” Umahi said. The minister added that his comments about Obi were a response to what he described as a pattern of condemning others. “I only said that when you continually condemn others, you bring judgment upon yourself,” he said. Umahi also faulted Obi for allegedly failing to caution some of his supporters over comments he considered offensive to Christians. He cited a remark reportedly made by one of Obi’s supporters that even if Jesus contested an election, Obi would win, describing it as an affront to the Christian faith. “One of them reportedly said that even if Jesus contested in an election, Peter Obi would win. That is an affront to our faith, and I expected Peter Obi to speak out against such a statement,” he said. The minister’s comments followed his criticism of Obi’s presidential credentials, arguing that the former Anambra governor was not the best candidate the South-East could produce. “Peter Obi is not the best of our finest in South-East,” Umahi said. “He’s not the best; he can never be the best.” Umahi maintained that his position was not motivated by personal differences with Obi, but by his belief that the region had other qualified political figures who could pursue the presidency. The former Ebonyi State governor argued that anyone seeking to represent the South-East’s political interests at the national level should first consult governors and other influential leaders in the region. “You cannot play politics in South-East without consulting people like us,” he said. Umahi said building consensus among regional stakeholders was important for anyone seeking to advance a presidential ambition on behalf of the South-East. item.title: Man United goalie Onana rushed to hospital after car accident in Turkey
item.description: Manchester United goalkeeper Andre Onana was taken to hospital following a car accident in Turkey after Trabzonspor’s 2-0 victory over Hearts in the Conference League on Thursday. The Cameroon international was reportedly rear-ended by another vehicle, with images from the scene appearing to show debris from the collision. Onana was taken to hospital for medical checks but was later discharged after the results came back clear. Trabzonspor president Ertugrul Dogan confirmed the incident while providing an update on the goalkeeper’s condition. “Andre Onana was involved in a road traffic accident earlier this evening. There are no problems with him, and we wish him a speedy recovery,” as reported by GOAL. Onana has made an impressive start to life at the Turkish club, where he is spending a second spell on loan from Manchester United. The 30-year-old started Thursday’s victory over Hearts, which followed Trabzonspor’s 4-2 win over Finnish side KuPS. The result also marked his fourth clean sheet in five games for the club. Trabzonspor have enjoyed a strong run of form in recent weeks, defeating Turkish heavyweights Besiktas and Galatasaray by an aggregate score of 6-0. The team will return to league action against Rizespor next Monday, giving Onana time to rest and recover before the fixture, depending on his condition following the accident. Onana joined Manchester United from Inter Milan in the summer of 2023 for £43.8 million but struggled to establish himself consistently during his time at Old Trafford. His position at the club came under pressure following the arrival of goalkeeper Senne Lammens, prompting his temporary move to Trabzonspor. During his previous spell at Manchester United, Onana made 42 appearances and kept six clean sheets. However, his return to Trabzonspor has offered signs of improvement, with the goalkeeper already approaching that clean-sheet tally as his side continues its positive start to the season. item.title: Terrorism: FG secures 653 convictions, prosecutes 1,060 suspects
item.description: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri The Federal Government has secured a total of 653 convictions of persons arrested across the federation for their involvement in various acts of terrorism. The convicts, some of whom were found guilty of aiding insurgents or concealing information about their operations from security agencies, were among the 1,060 persons brought before the court in the third phase of the ongoing mass trial of terror suspects. Speaking to newsmen shortly after stepping out of the courtroom on Friday, the Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, Prince Lateef Fagbemi, SAN, who led the prosecution, disclosed that a total of 880 cases had been heard, out of which the court convicted 653, acquitted seven and discharged 27 of the defendants. He said the exercise would continue and the final figures would be announced after the conclusion of the trial. Describing the current phase of the mass trial as the largest since the FG commenced the special court sessions for the prosecution of terror suspects, the AGF attributed the success of the exercise to judicial cooperation, effective prosecution and inter-agency collaboration. He expressed appreciation to the judges handling the cases, particularly Justice Binta Nyako, who has been acting on behalf of the Chief Judge of the Federal High Court, Justice John Tsoho. The AGF also commended the prosecution team, the defence counsel and the security agencies for contributing to the smooth conduct of the proceedings. Among the agencies he acknowledged for their contributions were the Office of the National Security Adviser (NSA), the Department of State Services (DSS), the military, the police, correctional centres and the Legal Aid Council of Nigeria (LACoN). According to the AGF, collaboration among the institutions has been critical to advancing the prosecution of terrorism, terrorism financing and related offences in the country. On the representation of the defendants by lawyers from the LACoN, the AGF explained that the council was fulfilling its responsibility of providing legal assistance to eligible defendants. He clarified, however, that private legal practitioners were also representing some of the suspects. He said the defence lawyers were not only given the opportunity to interact with their clients before the court proceedings, but were also granted access to the detention facilities to enable them to prepare the defendants’ defence effectively. On the issue of deradicalisation of suspects recommended by the court, the AGF said the process remained an important component of the overall exercise. He maintained that rehabilitation and reintegration were necessary to complement the judicial process and reduce the risk of individuals returning to extremist activities. item.description: By Victor Ahiuma-Young The Nigeria Labour Congress, NLC, has clarified that the Trade Union Congress of Nigeria, TUC, neither issued an ultimatum to the Federal Government nor participated in the dialogue between the government and the NLC held on October 22, 2026. The clarification follows media reports that mentioned the TUC in connection with the ultimatum and the meeting, prompting the NLC to set the record straight and absolve the sister labour centre of any involvement in the specific engagement. The statement reads: “The Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) wishes to clarify that the Trade Union Congress (TUC) did not issue an ultimatum to the government and was not part of the dialogue between the NLC and Federal Government yesterday, 22nd October 2026 even as the TUC side of Joint Health Workers Union of Nigeria, JOHESU and Joint Public Service Negotiating Council, JPSNC were represented at the dialogue. “TUC’s name featured in error in a paper or two but we note that a greater number of the papers appropriately attributed the statement to NLC only. “This is to categorically state that only the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) was present at the meeting. “The TUC is completely exonerated from the purports of this specific dialogue. The clarification follows media reports that mentioned the TUC in connection with the ultimatum and the meeting, prompting the NLC to set the record straight and absolve the sister labour centre of any involvement in the specific engagement. In a statement signed by its Acting General Secretary, Comrade Benson Upah, the NLC said the TUC’s name was erroneously included in some newspaper reports, while acknowledging that a greater number of publications correctly attributed the statement to the NLC alone. The statement reads: “The Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) wishes to clarify that the Trade Union Congress (TUC) did not issue an ultimatum to the government and was not part of the dialogue between the NLC and Federal Government yesterday, 22nd October 2026 even as the TUC side of Joint Health Workers Union of Nigeria, JOHESU and Joint Public Service Negotiating Council, JPSNC were represented at the dialogue. “TUC’s name featured in error in a paper or two but we note that a greater number of the papers appropriately attributed the statement to NLC only. “This is to categorically state that only the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) was present at the meeting. “The TUC is completely exonerated from the purports of this specific dialogue. We urge the public and media to take note of this correction, please.” The post TUC not part of FG talks, issued no ultimatum, NLC clarifies appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Casualties Feared As Multi-Storey Building Collapses In Nairobi
item.description: A multi-storey building collapsed mid-construction in the Kenyan capital on Friday, the Red Cross said, with reports from local media of casualties and looting at the site. Videos spreading online showed a dramatic crash and huge clouds of dust as the building — thought to have been around 18 storeys high — came down in a densely populated business and residential area of Eastleigh. AFP journalists at the scene saw the building had been reduced to a pile of rubble as a small number of search and rescue teams arrived on the scene. “There were some businesses in the basement and workers who were busy building,” said local resident Abdi Aziz, 25. “But as it was (the Friday prayer), a lot of them were at the mosque. I think few people died because no one was living there,” he told AFP. Asked if he could see obvious flaws in the construction process, he said, “Everyone rushes to build in this neighbourhood.” This aerial view shows personnel from the Kenya Defence Forces Disaster Response Battalion inspecting the rubble of a collapsed residential building that was still under construction in the Eastleigh neighbourhood of Nairobi on October 23, 2026. (Photo by TONY KARUMBA / AFP) | TONY KARUMBA / AFP Local media reported looting and possible casualties trapped beneath the rubble, with images showing large crowds gathered at the site immediately after the incident, which happened around lunchtime. AFP saw police use tear gas to disperse crowds gathering near the site. Rescue operations had yet to begin when AFP arrived, with the site hemmed in by high-rise buildings, complicating efforts. Nairobi is undergoing a rapid construction boom, with high-rise buildings appearing all over the city, particularly in Eastleigh which is known for its busy market areas and as a hub for the Somali community. There have been many concerns over safety. There were 86 building collapses between 2009 and 2019, killing an estimated 200 people, according to a report by the Kenya Institute for Public Policy Research and Analysis. An audit of almost 15,000 buildings by the National Building Inspectorate found that 4.8 percent were very dangerous, 72.3 percent were classified as unsafe, the report said. The number of buildings completed annually in Nairobi has risen from 20,025 in 2022 to 25,090 last year, according to its statistics bureau, as east Africa’s leading business hub sucks in people from rural areas and neighbouring countries. item.title: Man Utd defeat to Como ‘unacceptable’, says Carrick
item.description: Manchester United manager Michael Carrick admitted on Friday his side have “lost their way” after a 4-1 thrashing by Champions League debutants Como made it seven games without a win. After a successful interim spell in charge in the second half of last season, Carrick was appointed on a permanent basis just five months ago, but his position is at risk ahead of Sunday’s visit of Bournemouth to Old Trafford. United are off to their worst start in the Premier League era, were dumped out of the League Cup by Brighton and have lost two of their opening three Champions League games. “Recently we haven’t had a good time. I totally accept that. We had five months of relative success in a spell where I was happy with a lot of things we were doing as a team,” Carrick said in an impassioned address at the start of his press conference on Friday. “We haven’t done well enough lately. We’ve had a spell we’re really not happy with. Como was a bad night. It hurt me. It was really unacceptable. “The supporters have to make the effort and spend the money to come and watch us. To have the feeling we all had after the game was a tough moment.” Carrick added: “My job is to put a team on the pitch that represents the supporters and that they can be proud of the identity we show. We have gone away from that recently in certain games which I am fully aware of and definintely doing something about.” AFP The post Man Utd defeat to Como ‘unacceptable’, says Carrick appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: I once wanted to be a DJ – UK’s Prince William
item.description: Prince William has made a rare royal appearance on a BBC chat show, with the heir to the throne confessing he would have liked to join the police or be a DJ. The Prince of Wales appeared on an episode set to air Friday evening, to promote his Earthshot Prize, which goes to environmental causes. The show’s host, comedian Graham Norton, is known for his A-list guests and mildly ribbing celebrities. Wearing a blue suit, shirt and tie, William was roaring with laughter in images released ahead of the show on his and his wife’s Instagram. He sat on the show’s sofa next to actresses Cate Blanchett and Hannah Waddingham and conservationist Robert Irwin, all involved in the prize. Hello! magazine wrote that William is the first working royal to appear on a British talk show although Sarah Ferguson, the former wife of William’s uncle, the former prince Andrew, was interviewed by Norton when she still had a royal title. The Graham Norton Show is now in its 33rd series and is the broadcaster’s most watched chat show. Recent guests include Madonna. The BBC reported there were “cheers and gasps from the audience” when William appeared as a surprise guest. He will present the Earthshot Prize in Mumbai on November 17. Launched in 2020, the prize supports initiatives that help tackle environmental crises such as climate change. As with previous competitions, this year’s winners will receive one million pounds ($1.3 million) each “to accelerate the impact of their innovative solutions”, organisers said. William was asked whether he ever fantasised about another job rather than becoming king, telling Norton: “I did want to be a policeman when I was younger. I thought I could make a good one,” adding that he also went through “a phase of wanting to be a DJ — I wasn’t very good.” William spoke of his family’s love for “The Celebrity Traitors”, a devious reality show currently topping ratings. He also said he was a “big fan” of director Christopher Nolan’s “Dark Knight” trilogy about Batman, which he called “psychologically dark and deep”. The prince has kept tight-lipped about the return to Britain of his estranged brother Prince Harry, who said in an interview this week with GQ magazine that he wanted things to “work out” with his father, King Charles III, and William, his elder brother. item.title: Malaria: Nigeria’s prevalence drops to 15.2%, FG targets 50% reduction by 2030
item.description: By Chioma Obinna The Federal Government has reported a decline in malaria parasite prevalence among children aged six to 59 months from 22 per cent in 2021 to 15.2 per cent in 2025, while setting a target to halve malaria prevalence and malaria-attributable deaths by 2030. The Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Prof. Muhammad Ali Pate, disclosed this on Thursday at the launch of the 2025 Nigeria Malaria Indicator Survey (NMIS) Report and the National Malaria Strategic Plan 2026–2030 in Abuja. Pate, who was represented by the ministry’s Permanent Secretary, Daju Kachollom, said the 6.8 percentage-point decline reflected progress in the country’s malaria control efforts but warned that the gains must be sustained. He said the Federal Government was targeting a 50 per cent reduction in malaria prevalence and malaria-attributable deaths from their respective 2025 levels by 2030. The minister, however, cautioned against interpreting the decline as evidence that malaria had been brought under control nationwide, stressing the need for stronger prevention, surveillance and funding. He cited Kebbi State as an example of significant improvement, with malaria prevalence reportedly dropping from 49 per cent in 2021 to 18 per cent in 2025. Pate said the findings underscored the importance of using reliable data to identify high-burden communities and direct interventions where they would have the greatest impact. Bed-net use remains a concern The minister also highlighted the need to improve the consistent use of insecticide-treated nets, a major tool for preventing malaria transmission. According to the survey findings, 72.3 per cent of children and 80.6 per cent of pregnant women in households that owned insecticide-treated nets slept under one. item.title: Ogogo’s daughters announce Nollywood plans, pledge to sustain father’s legacy
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye The daughters of late Nollywood actor Taiwo Hassan, popularly known as Ogogo, say they plan to pursue careers in the film industry and continue their father’s legacy. Taiwo Halima Olamide, known as Lima Ogogo, and her sister, Shakirat Taiwo, popularly called Kira Ogogo, announced their plans in an appreciation video shared on social media on Wednesday, October 21. The sisters also thanked Nigerians and members of the entertainment industry for supporting their family following their father’s death. “You guys loved our daddy so much. This is an appreciation video to tell you people thank you,” they said. Lima, speaking on behalf of the family, added: “On behalf of my family and I, we want to say thank you very much to everybody who stood by us.” The sisters acknowledged support from several public figures, including Honourable Tayo Ayinde, the First Lady, the Ogun State governor, Senator Solomon Olamilekan Adeola, popularly known as Yayi, and the Olu of Ilaro. They also thanked those who sent messages of condolence during the family’s period of mourning. They said their entry into Nollywood would be a lasting commitment, rather than a one-off tribute to their father. “We are going to start seeing Ogogo through my sister Kira Ogogo. We are coming to the industry, and we’re here to stay,” Lima said. The sisters urged fans who enjoyed Ogogo’s films to support their upcoming projects by watching and sharing their content, particularly on Kira Ogogo’s YouTube channel, KiraOgogoTV. Ogogo, a prominent figure in Yoruba cinema, died on August 23, 2026, aged 66. He was buried the following day in Ilaro, Ogun State, according to Islamic rites. His death drew tributes from Nollywood colleagues and admirers. The post Ogogo’s daughters announce Nollywood plans, pledge to sustain father’s legacy appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: FG Designates Redeemer’s Health Village As TETFund Centre, Guarantees Scholarships For Robotic Surgery Academy
item.description: In a breakthrough for Nigeria’s healthcare sector, the Federal Government has adopted the newly inaugurated Redeemer’s Health Village (RHV) Robotic Surgery Academy as the nation’s 29th TETFund Centre of Excellence, guaranteeing full scholarship coverage for all enrolled trainees. Speaking at the official inauguration on Thursday, Minister of Education Dr. Tunji Alausa declared that the Tertiary Education Trust Fund (TETFund) will fully fund the tuition fees of qualified medical professionals undergoing specialist training at the academy through its local scholarship scheme. ﻿ The strategic partnership — established alongside RoboMed Global, the National Postgraduate Medical College of Nigeria (NPMCN), and Redeemer’s University — establishes Nigeria’s pioneer institute for advanced robotic and telesurgical operations. ₦250bn Healthcare Injection Highlighting the government’s drive to curb brain drain and eliminate foreign medical tourism, Alausa disclosed that the Federal Government has injected over ₦250 billion into medical education across the last two years. “The same number of medical students admitted while I was in medical school is the same number we have maintained over the years, without sufficient consideration of our population growth,” the minister stated, confirming plans to expand annual medical programme enrolments to 20,000 within two years. By designating RHV as a Special Centre of Excellence, TETFund sponsorship will ensure that financial barriers do not stop top clinical talent from acquiring cutting-edge surgical skills locally. $4m Infrastructure The newly launched academy hits the ground running with $4 million worth of dual robotic surgical systems, designed to power both clinical service delivery and high-level training. According to RHV Chief Executive Officer Adedamola Dada, the academy aims to produce 400 certified specialists within two years across three main specialties: Urology, General Surgery, and Gynaecology. The academy’s scope extends beyond doctors to train an entire technical ecosystem, including operating theatre personnel, biomedical engineers, and hospital administrators. RHV also recently achieved full accreditation as an academic medical school. item.title: Indonesia’s Haze Crisis Raises Accountability Demands On Corporate Firms
item.description: After months of fires in Indonesia that have caused thick regional haze, attention is turning to whether companies can be held accountable for the blazes and resulting air pollution. Indonesia regularly experiences fires during its dry season, and experts say years of deforestation and peatland drainage for cultivation have left previously fire-resistant landscapes vulnerable. Driven by a strong El Nino cycle and resulting drought, this year’s blazes have been particularly severe, burning through nearly two million hectares, according to deforestation monitor Nusantara Atlas. The fires have raged across forests and peatland but also palm oil and timber plantations supplying multinational firms. Environmental group WALHI says it mapped “high confidence” hotspots across Indonesia using NASA fire data and found around 50 percent were inside concessions. In a report this month the group listed 40 timber and palm oil concessions by the number of hotspots detected. “This is a structural issue… (that) happens because of the practices, the activities, of these companies,” WALHI forests and plantations campaigner Umi Ma’rufah told AFP. Civil society groups have regularly accused companies of responsibility for the blazes, pointing to so-called “hotspots” in supplier plantations, sometimes called concessions. Demonstrators wearing gas masks hold protest placards outside China’s embassy to demand an audit of supply chains linked to Indonesian forest fires, in Jakarta on October 22, 2026. (Photo by BAY ISMOYO / AFP) Pressure is also coming from governments, including Singapore, which has issued 10 companies with “preventative measure notices” under its Transboundary Haze Pollution Act. The notices urge them to fight fires on their land, prevent burning and submit action plans. Firms can face legal action including fines if they do not comply. “We must also be clear about where the responsibility for this lies,” Singapore Senior Minister K. The fires have raged across forests and peatland but also palm oil and timber plantations supplying multinational firms. Environmental group WALHI says it mapped “high confidence” hotspots across Indonesia using NASA fire data and found around 50 percent were inside concessions. In a report this month the group listed 40 timber and palm oil concessions by the number of hotspots detected. “This is a structural issue… (that) happens because of the practices, the activities, of these companies,” WALHI forests and plantations campaigner Umi Ma’rufah told AFP. Civil society groups have regularly accused companies of responsibility for the blazes, pointing to so-called “hotspots” in supplier plantations, sometimes called concessions. Demonstrators wearing gas masks hold protest placards outside China’s embassy to demand an audit of supply chains linked to Indonesian forest fires, in Jakarta on October 22, 2026. (Photo by BAY ISMOYO / AFP) Pressure is also coming from governments, including Singapore, which has issued 10 companies with “preventative measure notices” under its Transboundary Haze Pollution Act. The notices urge them to fight fires on their land, prevent burning and submit action plans. Firms can face legal action including fines if they do not comply. “We must also be clear about where the responsibility for this lies,” Singapore Senior Minister K. Shanmugam told reporters. “This was not simply an act of nature, but a problem driven by companies pursuing profits.” Legal liability Several companies implicated have insisted they are not behind the fires. “Fires originating outside our boundaries subsequently spread into areas under the Group’s management,” Singapore Exchange-listed palm oil company First Resources said after one of its concessions was listed in WALHI’s report. Asia Pulp and Paper, a Singapore-registered firm, also insisted that fires in supplier concessions do not “necessarily mean that land was deliberately burned or that the concession holder was responsible for starting the fire.” Satellite monitoring can sometimes show where fires started, said Nusantara Atlas founder David Gaveau. “In some cases, the satellite photos clearly show that fire starts inside, but we cannot say whether it’s by design or whether it’s accidental,” he told AFP. “In other cases it’s also clear that fire started outside and spread inside the concession.” Experts say fire has been used in the past to illegally open up land for cultivation, including in large concessions, but also by smaller-scale local investors. Parts of Indonesia also previously allowed smallholders to use fire to clear plots of land, though this year the government has cracked down on that practice too. Even if fires begin accidentally or outside concessions, firms may have legal responsibilities, explained Azam Hawari, a lawyer with environmental law NGO ClientEarth. “An external source of ignition or extreme weather does not necessarily absolve a company of civil liability,” said Hawari. Companies are required to have sufficient fire measures, including personnel and equipment, and could also be liable “where activities pose a serious threat to the environment,” like peatland drainage, he added. International links Indonesia has announced “administrative sanctions” against dozens of firms and criminal proceedings against 125 individuals and corporations. But campaigner Umi pointed out that some previously prosecuted firms have failed to pay fines or carry out forest restoration. “It’s about the will from the government to really do their (enforcement) task,” she said. Some implicated concessions have ties well behind Indonesia’s borders, said Holly Yang, an accounting professor at Singapore Management University who teaches sustainability reporting. After WALHI’s report, she and her student Ashmit Bansal mapped concession holders, owners, creditors, investors and supply-chain partners. “The fires occur in Indonesia, but the ownership, financing and commercial relationships extend across borders,” Yang told AFP. Yang noted that a connection “does not, by itself, establish responsibility for a fire”. But mapping relationships “allows the public to ask informed questions and assess how those parties respond”. item.title: Emergency Nurseries Rescue DR Congo’s Ebola Orphans
item.description: A caregiver wore a protective gown and gloves as she bottle-fed a baby — one of hundreds of children orphaned by the Democratic Republic of Congo’s Ebola outbreak. With the disease still spreading five months into the epidemic, the nursery in the remote east is one of 12 receiving the children of those killed by the highly contagious haemorrhagic fever. “Many children have lost both their father and mother because of Ebola,” Marie Bakikula, a caregiver at a UNICEF-supported nursery in Mongbwalu, told AFP. The mining town in Ituri province near the Uganda border is considered the epicentre of the outbreak. Children account for about one-third of deaths and more than one-quarter of infections in the current crisis — more than 2,000 cases, according to UNICEF. A short distance from the nursery, workers in white protective suits loaded a child-sized coffin into the back of a pickup truck. Others survive but lose their families. Ebola orphans arriving at the emergency nurseries have seen their parents die and burial teams in protective suits come to remove the bodies. Others were separated from their families after their parents, infected with the virus, were transferred to Ebola treatment centres. “They all believe that by coming here they will never see their parents again,” said Monique Ndjangosi, a psychologist at the Mongbwalu nursery. item.title: One Dead, Three Rescued As Building Collapses In Lagos
item.description: One person has been confirmed dead and three others injured after a building collapsed in the Fadeyi area of Lagos State. The incident occurred on Akinola Street, off Ikorodu Road, on Friday morning. An emergency response team carries out a search-and-rescue operation with an excavator at the scene of a building collapse in Lagos State on October 23, 2026. The Lagos State Emergency Management Agency (LASEMA) said that while the cause of the collapse has yet to be ascertained, emergency responders are making frantic efforts to ascertain the number of people (on-site workers) trapped beneath the collapsed structure. An emergency response team carries out a search-and-rescue operation with an excavator at the scene of a building collapse in Lagos State on October 23, 2026. LASEMA said emergency responders have begun a coordinated search of the incident scene to ensure the prompt rescue of victims trapped under the collapsed building. It also noted that it is managing the incident scene to ensure a successful operation in collaboration with stakeholders, including the LRU paramedics, Lagos State Fire Service, LASASA and the Alabama Division of the Nigeria Police Force.
